guide.summaryTitle: About this puzzle: domains, methodology & FAQ
guide.frameworkRule: This puzzle evaluates abstract pattern recognition, sequence deduction, logic, and matrix reasoning using ten language-neutral questions. The final score is the count of correct answers out of ten and is not a clinical or standardized test.
guide.frameworkBoundary: Standardized clinical assessments require comprehensive multi-factor subtests and supervised psychometric administration. This tool is designed purely for cognitive practice and intellectual enjoyment.
guide.domainPatternDesc: Identifying invariant structural rules and transformations across abstract geometric shapes.
guide.domainSequenceDesc: Inferring progressive arithmetic steps, alternating intervals, and numeric series logic.
guide.domainLogicDesc: Evaluating relational rules to eliminate inconsistent possibilities and reach valid conclusions.
guide.domainSpatialDesc: Analyzing positional rotation, symmetry, and matrix placement of elements.
guide.scoreHighDesc: Strong fluid pattern synthesis and inductive rule deduction across varied problem types.
guide.scoreModerateDesc: Solid conceptual grasp of direct sequences and basic symbol symmetries with minor oversights on complex shifts.
guide.scoreFoundationDesc: An opportunity to practice non-verbal problem solving, deliberate rule elimination, and systematic scanning.
guide.faq1Q: Q: Is this an official score?
guide.faq1A: A: No. Standardized testing requires extensive clinical batteries with calibrated demographic cohorts. This is a lightweight educational puzzle measuring accuracy on ten abstract items.
guide.faq2Q: Q: Why are the questions language-neutral?
guide.faq2A: A: By using only abstract geometric shapes, matrices, and numbers, the puzzles minimize linguistic and cultural biases, focusing on fluid reasoning across all 12 supported languages.
guide.faq3Q: Q: What cognitive skills are involved?
guide.faq3A: A: The tasks tap into fluid reasoning, working memory strategies, pattern completion, and deductive elimination.
guide.faq4Q: Q: Can puzzle performance improve with practice?
guide.faq4A: A: Yes. Regular engagement with abstract logic puzzles trains working memory strategies, structured hypothesis testing, and attention to subtle visual transformations.
guide.faq5Q: Q: Are my test responses private?
guide.faq5A: A: Completely private. All calculations run client-side in your web browser. Individual answers and scores are never transmitted or stored on external servers.
